description: §14.8.9 — a server function in a `protect=` app that hand-builds its own `Response` fires E-PROTECT-005 (error). The compiler owns the egress envelope and mediates it (`_scrml_protect_redact` reads each value's protected-origin descriptor); it cannot mediate a body the author already serialized, because a `Response` is an opaque stream and the descriptor does not survive the author's own `JSON.stringify`. Fail-closed at compile time rather than fail-open on the wire.
rationale: §14.8.9 closed-world precondition: soundness rests on every construction being compiler-emitted and descriptor-preserving. An author-constructed `Response` breaks that precondition at the sink itself, so the compiler refuses to emit an envelope it cannot mediate. This is DELIBERATELY a hard error with NO escape hatch — `reveal("col")` does not discharge it, because reveal declassifies a column at a value the floor can still walk and a hand-serialized Response is not walkable. The removed capability is the argument for a future typed, mediatable return. ⚑ S441 (`g-protected-column-escapes-redaction-as-scalar`): `I-PROTECT-STRIP-001` no longer co-fires here, because nothing is stripped — the info now fires only for a query whose row the egress sink ACTUALLY stripped (the §14.8.9 provenance flow, `compiler/src/codegen/protect-flow.ts`). Before S441 it fired for every protected SELECT, and this case pinned that false claim. (The row goes into the author's own `JSON.stringify` body, which the runtime floor refuses; `E-PROTECT-006` also names the serialized protected column.)
